newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 97 CPI POSSIBLE ON SLOWER FOOD PRICES RISE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 97 CPI POSSIBLE ON SLOWER FOOD PRICES RISE.

text.p: The slow growth of food prices in the first two-months of this year may put Poland's 1997 ambitious 13-percent year-on-year inflation target within reach, a senior government analyst said on Friday.
Tadeusz Chroscicki, chief analyst at the government's Centre for Strategic Studies said food prices were likely to rise no more than 0.5 percent in February after a 1.2 percent rise in January.
"The growth of food prices is clearly slower than that of other goods and services, which lowers the overall consumer price index," Chroscicki told Reuters.
"The results of the first two months indicate that for the first time the inflation target (13-percent in year-on-year terms) in the budget law may not differ from reality," he said.
He said that food price growth is likely to slow down to 16.2 percent in February in year-on-year terms from 17.7 percent in January.

Chroscicki predicted the year-on-year food price index would drop to 14.2 percent in March and to 11 percent in June while the overall consumer price index is not likely to ease below 16 percent in that period from 18.1 percent in January.
